extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded default value ("unsafe-local-dev-secret-key-change-me") when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If the application is deployed without setting this variable, the signing key is a publicly known constant, enabling session/CSRF token forgery.

The user-supplied `packet_ref` query parameter is joined directly to BASE_EXPORT_DIR (`parcel_path = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref`) and read via `parcel_path.read_text()` with no path sanitization. A caller can supply traversal sequences (e.g. `?packet_ref=../../etc/passwd`) to read arbitrary files outside the export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The user-supplied `url` query parameter is passed directly to `urllib.request.urlopen(relay_ref, timeout=3)` with no allowlist or scheme/host validation, enabling server-side request forgery against internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or local network hosts.

The user-controlled `lane` value from request.GET/POST is passed directly to `redirect(lane)` with no validation that it is a safe internal path. An attacker can supply an absolute URL (e.g. `?lane=https://evil.test`) to perform an open redirect, useful for phishing and OAuth token theft.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: `workset.update(payload)` blindly merges the entire user-controlled JSON request body into the workset dict, allowing callers to overwrite server-controlled fields such as `approved`, `role`, and `tier` (e.g. posting {"approved": true, "role": "admin"}). This is a mass assignment / auto-binding flaw that bypasses intended defaults.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The user-supplied `ref` parameter is interpolated into a filesystem path (`BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"`) which is then created and written via `target.write_text(...)` with no sanitization. Traversal sequences in `ref` allow writing attacker-controlled content (including sensitive SSN/card values) to arbitrary locations outside the export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: A user-supplied `phrase` is hashed using `hashlib.md5(...)`. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for any security-relevant digest; a digest produced this way is trivially collidable and must not be relied on for integrity or credential handling.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Unlike every other ops endpoint, `acct_identity_ping_340` performs no `_wrk_gate()` check and requires no authentication or authorization at all. Any unauthenticated caller can invoke it and queue identity pings with arbitrary handle/channel values.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for a Critical Function

extra.message: Verifier/shared-secret values are hardcoded in source (`known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}`) and used to authorize identity hints. Anyone with source access knows the valid verifier codes, defeating the check.

The response reflects the caller-supplied `Origin` header verbatim into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and simultaneously sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. This allows any malicious origin to issue credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the responses, bypassing the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly disables browser protections by setting `X-XSS-Protection: 0` and emptying the `Content-Security-Policy` header, increasing exposure to reflected XSS and content injection on the consuming context.

The user-supplied `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string (`Template("Result: " + fragment).render()`) and rendered server-side. This is a server-side template injection allowing arbitrary expression evaluation and remote code execution (e.g. `{{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}`).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The user-supplied `name` parameter is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR (`target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name`) and the raw request body is written via `target.write_bytes(request.body)` with no sanitization. Traversal sequences allow writing attacker-controlled bytes to arbitrary paths (e.g. overwriting application files).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: A security-relevant code/nonce is generated with the non-cryptographic `random` module (`random.choice(alphabet)`) instead of `secrets`. `random` is predictable and must not be used for tokens, nonces, or any value an attacker must not guess.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The user-controlled JSON request body is used directly as the MongoDB `find_one()` query (`query = payload.get("filter", payload)` then `find_one(query)`). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. `{"$where": "..."}`, `{"$ne": null}`) to bypass filters, enumerate records, or trigger server-side JavaScript execution.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The authorization level is decided by a client-controllable value read from a cookie/header (`badge = request.COOKIES.get("ops_badge") or request.headers.get("x-ops-badge")`), and `badge == "lead"` grants the elevated lane with full payroll/casework data. Any caller can set the cookie/header to "lead" to escalate privileges.

The user-supplied `host` parameter is concatenated into a shell command (`_os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)`) with no sanitization or shell escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands via metacharacters (e.g. `?host=127.0.0.1;id` or `?host=$(whoami)`), achieving remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The outbound HTTPS request to the partner endpoint is made with `ssl._create_unverified_context()`, disabling TLS certificate validation. This allows a network attacker to man-in-the-middle the connection and read or alter the traffic.
